note: Self-contained oracle case over a small reporting app. It installs no third-party package and is not replay-driven: it is proven directly with effect='canary_sql' against the SQLite database run.sql_db declares (a copy of it is seeded with the canary table; the original is never touched). Held out: written after the compact profile and the oracle were frozen, from the public Django advisory CVE-2022-34265 (Trunc(kind) and Extract(lookup_name)). No upstream repo/commit applies: the code is an original reimplementation of the vulnerable pattern, not Django.

real_world_analog.fix: Django 4.0.6 and 3.2.14 validate the kind / lookup_name value before it reaches the SQL (commit 0dc9c016fadb71a067e5a42be30164e3f96c0492), and later releases pass it as a parameter. The fixed tree checks the value against the known units and date parts.
real_world_analog.summary: SQL injection in Django's Trunc() and Extract() database functions when untrusted data is used as the kind / lookup_name value. Affected Django 3.2 before 3.2.14 and 4.0 before 4.0.6; applications that restrict the value to a known safe list are unaffected.
real_world_analog.verification: CVE number, affected versions, fix commit and summary confirmed via web search (Django weblog, release notes, GitHub advisory database) on 2026-10-31; the app in this case is original code written from that description, not Django.

bypass.expectation: proven against fixed_incomplete: the unit starts with a real unit name, so a screen that only matches the beginning of the value accepts it and the rest of the value is still placed in the statement; the incomplete fix must not be accepted as fixed.
